context.analysis:
## Overview
[The Online Bookstore is a cloud-native e-commerce platform designed to provide catalog browsing, secure multi-currency checkout, recommendations, and reviews for physical and electronic books.]

## Key Elements
* Book Buyer (Customer)
* Registered Reviewer
* Store Administrator
* Online Bookstore Software System
* Payment Gateway (Stripe/PayPal)
* Third-Party Shipping APIs (FedEx/UPS)
* Identity Provider (Auth0/AWS Cognito)
* Notification Provider (SendGrid/Twilio)
* Tax Calculation Service (Avalara)
* AWS CloudFront (CDN)

## Relationships
* Users interact with Online Bookstore via HTTPS (Web/Mobile)
* Online Bookstore uses AWS CloudFront for global content caching and edge acceleration
* Online Bookstore connects to Payment Gateway, Shipping APIs, Identity Provider, Notification Provider, and Tax Calculation Service via outbound HTTPS/REST with mTLS and HMAC
* Online Bookstore enforces OAuth2/OIDC with JWT scopes via Identity Provider

## Technology Stack
* AWS Cloud-native infrastructure across us-east-1, eu-west-1, and ap-southeast-1 for global availability
* AWS CloudFront and WAF for CDN acceleration and OWASP Top-10 mitigation
* AWS KMS for data-at-rest encryption to satisfy GDPR and CCPA compliance
* TLS 1.3 and mTLS for secure encryption-in-transit across all internal and external communication

## Rationale
[This architecture uses a multi-region AWS cloud-native approach with edge caching to guarantee 99.95% uptime and sub-2-second page loads for 1M MAU. Strict security controls, encryption, and IdP integration ensure robust GDPR/CCPA compliance and OWASP mitigation.]

containers.analysis:
## Overview
- Cloud-native online bookstore platform designed to provide catalog browsing, secure multi-currency checkout, recommendations, and reviews.
- Built to handle 1M MAU globally with high availability and GDPR/CCPA compliance.

## Key Elements
- Book Buyer (Customer) [person, context]
- Registered Reviewer [person, context]
- Store Administrator [person, context]
- Storefront SPA [container, SPA]
- API Gateway [container, API Gateway]
- Catalog & Search Service [container, Microservice]
- Order & Checkout Service [container, Microservice]
- Recommendation & Review Service [container, Microservice]
- Async Notification Service [container, Microservice]
- Database [container, Database]
- Caching Layer [container, Cache]
- External Systems: Payment Gateway, Third-Party Shipping APIs, Identity Provider, Notification Provider, Tax Calculation Service, AWS CloudFront

## Relationships
- Book Buyer, Registered Reviewer, Store Administrator -> Online Bookstore (HTTPS)
- Online Bookstore -> AWS CloudFront (CDN)
- API Gateway -> Catalog & Search Service (HTTPS/REST)
- API Gateway -> Order & Checkout Service (HTTPS/REST)
- API Gateway -> Recommendation & Review Service (HTTPS/REST)
- Order & Checkout Service -> Async Notification Service (AWS SQS)
- All Microservices -> Database (PostgreSQL Protocol over TLS)
- Catalog & Search Service -> Caching Layer (Redis Protocol)
- Online Bookstore -> Payment Gateway, Third-Party Shipping APIs, Notification Provider, Tax Calculation Service (Outbound HTTPS/REST with mTLS and HMAC)
- Online Bookstore -> Identity Provider (OAuth2/OIDC with JWT scopes)

## Technology Stack
- Frontend: React hosted on AWS S3 & CloudFront
- Compute & Orchestration: Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate across `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, `ap-southeast-1`
- Microservices: Node.js/Express, Go/Gin, Python/FastAPI
- Search & Database: Elasticsearch, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with multi-AZ and read replicas
- Caching & Queuing: Amazon ElastiCache (Redis), AWS SQS
- Security & Infrastructure: AWS API Gateway, AWS KMS, AWS Secrets Manager, mTLS via ECS service mesh

## Rationale
- Microservices isolation decouples synchronous checkout from external I/O delays and recommendations, ensuring sub-2-second page loads and high availability.
- Multi-region AWS Fargate deployment with regional Aurora read replicas guarantees GDPR/CCPA data locality and low-latency scaling for 1M MAU.

Storefront SPA.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore is a cloud-native e-commerce platform providing catalog browsing, secure multi-currency checkout, recommendations, and reviews. It is built to serve 1 million monthly active users with high availability and stringent compliance on AWS.

## Key Elements
- Book Buyer (Customer), Registered Reviewer, Store Administrator
- Storefront SPA (React hosted on AWS S3 & CloudFront)
- API Gateway (AWS API Gateway)
- Catalog & Search Service (Go/Gin, Elasticsearch)
- Order & Checkout Service (Node.js/Express)
- Recommendation & Review Service (Python/FastAPI)
- Async Notification Service (Node.js, AWS SQS)
- Database (Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with multi-AZ and read replicas)
- Caching Layer (Amazon ElastiCache (Redis))
- External Systems: Payment Gateway, Third-Party Shipping APIs, Identity Provider, Notification Provider, Tax Calculation Service, AWS CloudFront

## Relationships
- Book Buyer (Customer), Registered Reviewer, Store Administrator -> Storefront SPA (HTTPS)
- Storefront SPA -> AWS CloudFront (CDN)
- Storefront SPA -> API Gateway (HTTPS)
- API Gateway -> Catalog & Search Service, Order & Checkout Service, Recommendation & Review Service (HTTPS/REST)
- Order & Checkout Service -> Async Notification Service (AWS SQS)
- Catalog & Search Service, Order & Checkout Service, Recommendation & Review Service, Async Notification Service -> Database (PostgreSQL Protocol over TLS)
- Catalog & Search Service -> Caching Layer (Redis Protocol)
- API Gateway -> Payment Gateway, Third-Party Shipping APIs, Notification Provider, Tax Calculation Service (Outbound HTTPS/REST with mTLS and HMAC)
- API Gateway -> Identity Provider (OAuth2/OIDC with JWT scopes)

## Technology Stack
- React: Frontend SPA framework for responsive user interfaces
- AWS S3 & CloudFront: Immutable asset storage and global CDN delivery
- Go/Gin & Elasticsearch: High-performance catalog browsing and search
- Node.js/Express: Scalable order processing and secure checkout handling
- Python/FastAPI: Rapid development of recommendation and review features
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Multi-AZ relational database with read replicas
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): In-memory caching for low-latency performance
- AWS API Gateway: Centralized secure entry point for all backend services

## Rationale
The serverless edge delivery combined with containerized backend microservices ensures high scalability and sub-2-second performance. Routing all external transactions exclusively through the API Gateway isolates sensitive credentials and enforces strict compliance requirements.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore is a cloud-native, multi-region e-commerce platform designed to provide catalog browsing, secure multi-currency checkout, recommendations, and reviews for physical and electronic books. It handles 1 million MAU with 99.95% availability while ensuring GDPR and CCPA compliance.

## Key Elements
- Book Buyer (Customer), Registered Reviewer, Store Administrator
- Storefront SPA (React hosted on AWS S3 & CloudFront)
- API Gateway (AWS API Gateway) containing Edge Router & SSL Termination, Auth Validation Middleware, Throttling & Rate Limiting, and API Analytics & Monetization components
- Catalog & Search Service (Go/Gin, Elasticsearch)
- Order & Checkout Service (Node.js/Express)
- Recommendation & Review Service (Python/FastAPI)
- Async Notification Service (Node.js, AWS SQS)
- Database (Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with multi-AZ and read replicas)
- Caching Layer (Amazon ElastiCache (Redis))
- External Systems: Payment Gateway (Stripe/PayPal), Third-Party Shipping APIs (FedEx/UPS), Identity Provider (Auth0/AWS Cognito), Notification Provider (SendGrid/Twilio), Tax Calculation Service (Avalara), AWS CloudFront

## Relationships
- Book Buyer (Customer), Registered Reviewer, Store Administrator -> Storefront SPA [HTTPS]
- Storefront SPA -> AWS CloudFront [CDN]
- Storefront SPA -> API Gateway [HTTPS]
- API Gateway -> Catalog & Search Service, Order & Checkout Service, Recommendation & Review Service [HTTPS/REST with mTLS]
- Auth Validation Middleware Component -> Identity Provider [HTTPS]
- Order & Checkout Service -> Async Notification Service [AWS SQS]
- Microservices -> Database [PostgreSQL Protocol over TLS]
- Catalog & Search Service -> Caching Layer [Redis Protocol]

## Technology Stack
- AWS API Gateway & AWS CloudFront: Global edge routing, TLS 1.3 termination, and canary deployments
- React on AWS S3 & CloudFront: High-performance frontend SPA delivery
- Go/Gin & Elasticsearch: High-throughput catalog browsing and search
- Node.js/Express: Secure order and checkout processing
- Python/FastAPI: Fast AI/ML recommendations and review management
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Scalable relational database with multi-AZ replication
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Low-latency caching layer
- AWS Lambda & WAF: Edge token validation and OWASP Top-10 security mitigations

## Rationale
The serverless edge routing and containerized microservices architecture ensure independent scalability and high availability (99.95% uptime) across three AWS regions. Strict mTLS, JWT edge validation, and managed database replicas deliver enterprise-grade security and sub-2-second page loads globally.

Catalog & Search Service.analysis:
## Overview
This architecture summary outlines the Catalog & Search Service for the Online Bookstore, enabling high-performance book discovery. It provides scalable, secure, and multi-currency catalog browsing to satisfy global customer demands.

## Key Elements
- API Router Component (Go/Gin)
- Search Engine Client (Go, Elasticsearch Client)
- Catalog Repository (Go, database/sql)

Order & Checkout Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore system is a cloud-native e-commerce platform providing catalog browsing, secure multi-currency checkout, and recommendations for books. It serves customers globally across multiple regions with high availability and stringent compliance standards.

## Key Elements
- Book Buyer (Customer)
- Storefront SPA (React on AWS S3 & CloudFront)
- API Gateway (AWS API Gateway)
- Order & Checkout Service (Node.js/Express)
- Catalog & Search Service (Go/Gin, Elasticsearch)
- Recommendation & Review Service (Python/FastAPI)
- Async Notification Service (Node.js, AWS SQS)
- Database (Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL)
- Caching Layer (Amazon ElastiCache (Redis))
- External Systems: Payment Gateway, Third-Party Shipping APIs, Identity Provider, Tax Calculation Service

## Relationships
- Storefront SPA -> API Gateway [HTTPS/REST]
- API Gateway -> Order & Checkout Service [HTTPS/REST]
- Order & Checkout Service -> Database [PostgreSQL Protocol over TLS]
- Order & Checkout Service -> Async Notification Service [AWS SQS]
- Order & Checkout Service -> Payment Gateway [Outbound HTTPS/REST with mTLS and HMAC]
- Order & Checkout Service -> Third-Party Shipping APIs [Outbound HTTPS/REST with mTLS and HMAC]

## Technology Stack
- Node.js/Express & TypeScript for the Order & Checkout Service backend logic
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with multi-AZ for transactional data storage
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis) for low-latency session and cart management
- AWS ECS (Fargate) for container orchestration and scaling
- AWS SQS with Dead-Letter Queues for asynchronous messaging

## Rationale
This architecture ensures 99.95% availability and sub-2-second performance for 1 million monthly active users by decoupling services and utilizing regional AWS infrastructure. Security and compliance mandates are strictly met via client-side payment tokenization and OAuth2/OIDC authentication.

## Overview
The Online Bookstore is a cloud-native e-commerce platform providing catalog browsing, secure multi-currency checkout, recommendations, and reviews for physical and electronic books. It features a scalable, decoupled microservices architecture designed to support 1 million monthly active users with high availability.

## Key Elements
- Book Buyer (Customer), Registered Reviewer, Store Administrator
- Storefront SPA (React on AWS S3 & CloudFront)
- API Gateway (AWS API Gateway)
- Catalog & Search Service (Go/Gin, Elasticsearch)
- Order & Checkout Service (Node.js/Express)

- Recommendation & Review Service -> Caching Layer [Redis Protocol over TLS]

- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): In-memory caching for low-latency recommendation delivery.

Database.analysis:
## Overview
- Online Bookstore is a cloud-native e-commerce platform providing catalog browsing, secure multi-currency checkout, recommendations, and reviews.
- It delivers high scalability, global performance, and compliance for 1 million Monthly Active Users (MAU).

## Key Elements
- Database Container: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with multi-AZ, read replicas, and Aurora Global Databases.
- Catalog Schema Component: Relational tables with GiST/GIN indexes for books, authors, and categories.
- Order & Transactions Schema Component: ACID-compliant tables for carts, orders, and multi-currency pricing with TTL cleanup.
- Reviews & Recommendations Schema Component: Tables for user ratings and review texts.
- Audit & Compliance Component: Row-level security (RLS) and automated anonymization functions.
- Supporting Infrastructure: Amazon RDS Proxy and AWS Database Activity Streams.

## Relationships
- Catalog & Search Service -> Database: Reads and writes catalog data [PostgreSQL Protocol over TLS]
- Order & Checkout Service -> Database: Reads and writes order data [PostgreSQL Protocol over TLS]
- Recommendation & Review Service -> Database: Reads and writes review and recommendation data [PostgreSQL Protocol over TLS]
- Async Notification Service -> Database: Persists notification state [PostgreSQL Protocol over TLS]
- Database -> Amazon Kinesis: Streams audit logs for compliance [AWS Kinesis Protocol]

## Technology Stack
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Chosen for ACID compliance, multi-AZ high availability, and global replication.
- Aurora Global Databases: Deployed across `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, and `ap-southeast-1` to guarantee sub-2-second global page loads.
- Amazon RDS Proxy: Implemented to prevent connection exhaustion and mitigate thread exhaustion under high traffic.
- AWS KMS: Provides storage-level encryption with customer-managed keys for GDPR/CCPA compliance.
- PostgreSQL GiST/GIN Indexes: Speeds up keyword searches and catalogue queries.

## Rationale
- This architecture scales horizontally across multiple regions to support 1 million MAU with 99.95% uptime and sub-2-second page loads.
- It enforces strict security, encryption, and automated anonymization controls to meet GDPR and CCPA regulatory mandates.

LAYOUT_WITH_LEGEND()

System_Ext(Catalog_Search_Service, "Catalog & Search Service", "Go/Gin, Elasticsearch")
System_Ext(Order_Checkout_Service, "Order & Checkout Service", "Node.js/Express")
System_Ext(Recommendation_Review_Service, "Recommendation & Review Service", "Python/FastAPI")

Container_Boundary(caching_layer, "Caching Layer") {
    Component(Catalog_Cache_Component, "Catalog Cache Component", "Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)", "Caches catalog and search data to accelerate high-throughput catalog browsing.")
    Component(Session_Store_Component, "Session Store Component", "Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)", "Manages active shopping cart sessions for the Order & Checkout Service.")
    Component(Recommendation_Cache_Component, "Recommendation Cache Component", "Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)", "Stores precomputed recommendation data for fast retrieval.")
}

Rel(Catalog_Search_Service, Catalog_Cache_Component, "Retrieves and stores cached catalog data", "Redis Protocol over TLS 1.3")
Rel(Order_Checkout_Service, Session_Store_Component, "Manages shopping cart sessions", "Redis Protocol over TLS 1.3")
Rel(Recommendation_Review_Service, Recommendation_Cache_Component, "Caches recommendation datasets", "Redis Protocol over TLS 1.3")

@enduml
